messages.text: Dad, did Earl ever bring back your impact driver or is that still making the rounds?
He dropped it on the porch before lunch. I snapped the model tag before it went back on the shelf.
Good. I can swing by Saturday and help you put that new hasp on the side door.
Saturday works. I already told Earl by phone message to use the gate if he needs the socket set.
Can you and Mom FaceTime after dinner? The kids want to show her the school photos before you head out.
We can do 7:45. Linda has us doing the block first while it is still light.
Perfect. I will tell them. Also, do not let her skip writing it down for Dr. Harris.
She already put the pad by the back door next to our shoes.
Dad, Robbie's robotics group keeps burning through little LEDs. Could you look at his photo and tell him what to check first?
Have him pull the battery clip before touching it, then follow the wire from the long leg of the LED to the resistor. I can mark up a one-page sheet for him.
That would help. He listens better when he can see the steps instead of me guessing.
I'll draw it with a dead battery symbol and a simple meter check. Same kind of sheet I wanted for the community room kids.
Dad, Mateo wants to video call about the wobbly bookshelf. I told him you just talk us through stuff now and do not take envelopes for it.
That is fine. I can look at it on video after breakfast tomorrow, then I need to sort the sample parts for Saturday at the hall.
Perfect. He mostly wants to hear your voice and use the little level you gave him.
Good. Have him set the shelf empty first. No shortcuts with that kid.
I found that old box with Mom's papers. There is a blue county copy from Mesa and a faded envelope with the Apache Trail address.
Keep both, please. Linda wants me to get the names and dates straight before we send anything off.
I will. Also found a photo of us standing by that dusty wash behind the trailer, Dad holding the toolbox like always.
That sounds about right. Shade from the truck, water jug on the tailgate, and everybody fixing something before supper.
Albertsons here has that Tuesday 55+ line on the receipt. You and Linda should check yours before you load the cart.
Good reminder. I am grabbing beans, chicken thighs, eggs, and tortillas before the afternoon rush.
That sounds like Mom's table. She could turn one pot into three suppers.
I have a little smoked brisket frozen too, but that is for a Sunday plate, not every night.
I found that picture of us by Dad's old toolbox. You had the wrench and I was standing there with two front teeth missing.
That sounds about right. Send it when you get a chance.
I will. Also, the mornings here in Silver City are still cold, so do not trust the weather app if you two make the drive this spring.
I need to see what the truck says first. Linda and I will look at the calendar after bills.
You sounded wound tight on the phone. Did you ever get out to your bench?
I put the old radio on, cleaned up that little mesquite box, and touched up two chisels. Better than sitting at the table staring at bills.
That sounds like Dad after supper. Are you keeping that box or is it one of the extras?
Extra, maybe. If Ray still wants it, fine. I'm not making a list for anybody.
Saw the Bulldog Canyon post. Gate 10 looks washed out again.
I saw that too. Before we pick a route, I am watching that fellow show how he patched a cracked ATV fender with mesh and epoxy.
Good. My left knee votes for the smoother road anyway.
Same here. I saved the clip and the trail comments so I can look again after breakfast.
I can swing by from Mesa after my last rooftop unit. Probably 6:30 if traffic behaves.
Dad, neighbor here has a dryer that hums but won't spin. Belt maybe?
Found that old blue socket set in your garage. Same one from the Apache Junction carport photos?
That works. Linda is making enough for you, Erin, and all four little plates if everyone makes it.
Pretty sure. Dad kept it under the bench. Marlene used to hide her bike pump behind it so he would not toss it.
Could be belt, door switch, or motor start. Don't let him buy parts till somebody checks it with the back off and power pulled.
The box still smells like oil. Linda says the photo has Grandma in that white lunch apron too.
He asked what you'd charge just to look.
Mine are in. Erin said she is watching the clock at the front desk and will text when she gets out.
Tell him $35 to find the trouble. If it is a cheap belt, say so. Put a towel down before moving it or his wife will see every scrape.
That sounds like our old place. Tight little carport, but everything had a spot.
Good. I put the garage fan aside too, if you want to look at that capacitor before dinner.
Milo wants to show you the cardboard bridge before bedtime. He says the rubber band part finally works.
Tell him I will be in my chair after supper. I will set the tablet on the little stand.
Perfect. If he gets too excited, ask him to hold it closer to the camera so you can see the joint.
I want to see that part. Last time he moved it too fast and I missed the good bit.
Mom said you checked the dinner plan twice and then got sharp about the grocery total. Everything okay over there?
Dad, Riley's class has a family chart due Friday. Do you remember which side had the McKee name and which had Lancaster?
I was wound up about March bills and took it out on her. I went out to the garage and put the old Waylon tape on.
McKee was Mom's side, I think. Lancaster might be Dad's mother. Aunt Marlene keeps that straighter than I do.
Good. Maybe leave the spreadsheet closed tonight and look again tomorrow after breakfast.
No worries. The worksheet also asks what box you usually mark on school and doctor forms, but I can fill that from what Mom put last year.
That's the plan. Calendar says nothing due till Friday anyway.
Use the same one she used. I never remember the order on those forms, just the answer.
That clip you sent of John Denver in the green shirt made me remember Mom humming in the kitchen.
I let it play on the TV after supper. The next one had him with just a guitar and a stool.
Sounds like something Dad would have left on while sorting bolts.
Pretty much. I saved it so I can find it again without digging.
Saw two busted bottles and a torn-up cooler lid by the Goldfield wash turnoff this morning. Somebody left a mess.
I am adding that spot to my notes. Also marking where a second water jug makes sense before the sandy stretch.
Put in a line about folks packing out what they bring. Shouldn't need saying, but here we are.
I wrote it plain. Same page has the tire plug kit, small shovel, and when to turn around before heat gets stupid.
If you go north, skip that washed-out cut by Kayenta unless your truck tires are fresher than mine.
I was looking at 191 up through Chinle, then maybe 59 if the weather stays clean. Linda likes the quieter stretches.
Good. Watch the grade after Many Farms. There is a little marker pullout before Mexican Water if you two are stopping to read signs.
That is exactly the kind of stop I was circling. Not trying to make it all highway and gas receipts.
You going to the AJ hall thing Thursday? They said budget, new homes, and the police chief taking questions.
Probably. I want to hear the chief on cameras and training before I make up my mind on that council slate.
Same. Just don't let Erin send you 6 articles first or we'll be there all night.
Too late, she already sent two. I told her I would read them before shooting my mouth off.
Cookout Saturday. Want me to grab your usual fizzy waters or are you taking from the garage fridge?
I will bring a case of lime cans. Still have two of the three longnecks from last weekend, so no need to buy more for me.
Good. Cousin Ray is bringing his little pouch of party stuff again. I will keep it on the far table.
Fine by me. I am sticking with a clear head and driving Linda home before it gets late.
Bulldog Canyon is open Saturday. I was thinking one easy loop, skip the rocky wash.
That works. I'm bringing the black sleeve and calling it after the first loop.
Good. I'll leave the long route for the showoffs.
Fine by me. Still want to check the gate and trail trash while we're out there.
You still want that 10mm socket back or did it disappear behind the Christmas bins again?
Found it under the folding chairs. I am changing the truck oil after I tighten the hose bib.
Of course. Need me for the heavy stuff?
Maybe just swing by before lunch. I also have two drip heads by the ocotillo barely spitting.
Did you ever find that laminated page you made for the picture-sending lesson? I still use mine.
Found it in the toolbox drawer. Making 12 fresh copies tonight before Tuesday.
You have been hauling those folders over there since before my 2023 visit, I think.
Sounds right. Same room, different phones, more stubborn passwords.
Buckeye framing guy called me looking for hands. Two weeks, motel covered, decent check.
Tell him thanks, but I'm keeping to the little jobs around AJ this month. Linda has late shifts and I promised the kids I could grab them after school if needed.
Figured. You still doing that sink demo thing Tuesday morning?
Yep. Got three folks bringing photos of bad shutoffs. Better than sitting here sorting old screws.
Trail past Bulldog looked chewed up after that wind. Short loop tomorrow?
Short loop works. I already promised Ray I'd be at the hall this week, so I'm saving the knee.
Good. And if Leonard starts on Washington again Thursday, pretend you forgot your hearing aid 😄
I'll just count my points and let him talk to the wall.
You look at that county sheet yet? I got lost where they start talking road bonds and impact fees.
I marked the road piece and the water district one. Need to see who pays and what they actually fix.
Exactly. If they want more out of us, show the potholes getting filled.
I'm keeping the envelope on the counter until Linda and I finish the judge page tonight.
I can swing by at 7:30 for that condenser pad. Forecast jumps by 11.
Good. I'll have the brimmed cap and the thin sleeve shirt on before you get here.
Don't wear those newer boots if we're messing with gravel.
Already pulled the scratched pair. They'll look worse after ten minutes anyway.
I can swing by after the Mesa call. Leave that vise where it is.
Fine. I already moved the small drawers and quit before I got dumb about it.
Look at you reading the manual. I'll bring the hand truck.
I still want the bench cleared enough to finish sanding those shelf brackets.
I put the blue bottle by your keys and your tan hat on the chair.
Saw them. I am just doing the canal stretch and should be back before you leave.
Good. Please do the shorter turn today if it feels like too much. 🙂
That is the plan. No proving anything before breakfast.
I picked up corn tortillas and the little bag of dried chiles. Do you still want me to grab limes?
Yes please. I thawed the chicken and put the beans on. I can do the peppers outside once it cools off.
Good. I will bring cilantro too, but no extra chips this time. We still have salsa from Thursday.
That works. I will save the heavier stuff for when Brian comes over.
I put the Safeway and gas receipts by your chair. Walgreens was $14.20 today.
Thanks. After dinner I’ll match them against the bank screen and write the totals in both places.
Electric bill is due Friday, too. Please leave that $400 line alone unless we truly need it. 🙂
That’s the plan. I’ll mark the bill first, then the gas and grocery columns.
You rolling out this early or waiting for the sun to cook us?
Doing the short loop first. If the wash is firm, we can take the machines out after breakfast.
Good. I aired mine last night. No hero stuff on that rocky side trail.
Agreed. I want to be back while the east face still has that red on it anyway.
That 89A run still on, or did the heat scare you off?
Not heat. I left it unbooked after the plumber invoice showed up.
Makes sense. Easier to wander up there when the truck money is already set aside.
Exactly. I put a little aside on payday and keep the maps in the door pocket.
Dad, could you do a quick video call with Maya after dinner? Her birdhouse roof keeps sliding before the glue sets.
Dad, for the dental office sliding-scale sheet, they only need what hits the checking each month and copies of regular bills.
Tell her not to rush it. Dry fit first, then one thin line of glue. I can call at 7:10.
Okay. I have Linda's two Friday stubs, the Vanguard draw, that little monthly paper from the old job, and the house payment statement.
She saved the crooked piece because you told her not to toss wood until she knows it can't be used.
Good. Crooked pieces teach more than perfect ones if she checks the square and fixes what she can.
That should be enough. If they ask about food cards or rent letters, just mark none and don't overthink it.
Will do. Our monthly total still pencils out around $3,900 before the APS and water bills.
Queen Valley route is chewed up after the weekend. Want the shorter loop Saturday?
Shorter is smarter. Still carrying that right brace in the truck after the last rough ride.
Bring it. Also don't skip whatever little morning tablet Linda nags you about before we head out.
Already in the pill box. I am asking Dr. Patel's office Friday about that shot notice before I say yes to anything at the counter.
Dad, did you watch the clip I sent? I know your first reaction is usually about the officer having two seconds to decide.
I watched it twice. Still think the job has to be possible, but the stop looked sloppy and the report should not be the only record.
That's all I'm asking. Hear the family side before you lock in.
I am trying. Cameras, better practice, and somebody outside the chain reading the file would make sense to me.
You up by First Water again? Sky looked clean from my porch.
Yep. No engine today, just coffee and that ridge turning gold.
Better than the folding-chair hour Sunday?
Different kind of quiet. I need both when the week gets loud.
Ride Thursday morning or are you doing the room-with-the-long-tables thing again?
Thursday is copies from 8 to 9, people from 9:30 to 11, then I have to stack chairs.
So short loop after lunch, old man pace. Bring the knee brace.
That works. I will be dusty enough before we even hit the trail.
You two got the desert table again or is Mom making me sit by the laundry room door Sunday?
Depends if you keep stealing the last tortilla. Linda has you down for ice and maybe one folding chair from your garage.
Done. Also if the 6:40 game runs long, don't let Mom text me every bad call while I'm driving back to Mesa.
No promises. She already circled it on the TV guide.
I grabbed the extra inline fuse holders from the shop. You still want them for those little boards?
Yes. I want the first mistake to pop a cheap fuse, not scare anybody. Bring the crimper too if you can.
Got it. You meeting that retired plumber at the hall tonight?
At 6. He said two other old hands might sit in. I want them to see the boards before we ask the school counselor about a Saturday group.
You still want me there Sunday at 2? Mom said you moved it on the wall calendar then moved it back.
Yeah, 2 is right. I kept staring at the gas card bill and started messing with everything else.
I'm by Main and Stapley after my last call. Want me to swing past that Mesa counter before they close?
Leave the calendar alone, Dad. Go make noise in the garage for a bit.
Appreciate it, but I already handled it Saturday. Still need to sort the AJ boxes in the garage.
Already have the radio on. I will quit poking at it.
Those the ones with grandpa's old wrench roll and all the brittle maps?
Yes. Half of it is parts, receipts, and notes about which road washed out after a storm.
You still want me there Sunday for the shelves?
Yes. I can measure and hold boards, but you take the low cabinets.
Bring those blue pads from the garage. Tile floor will beat you up.
Already set them by the drill case. Same deal as the rides: shorter stretches, more breaks.
Mom said you had papers spread all over the table. Anything in there about police staffing?
There is a city line for that, plus county supervisor notes. I'm checking the dollar amounts before I seal anything.
Good. Same as a bid, numbers first.
And whether they are crowding shops off their own lots with that zoning change.
Dad, if that guy from the hall sends another link tonight, maybe just leave it unread until morning.
That's the plan. I'm going for the table, not the phone screen.
Good. Win a hand for me and don't let Ray make you keep score all night.
Ray can write for once. I have my pencil in the truck if he forgets.
Mom said you helped Mrs. Delgado with her porch latch, then went straight to Idaho Rd. Long day?
Not bad. Porch was ten minutes and close by. The center had me show a couple guys how to patch drywall without making a mountain of mud.
That sounds like a better use of your hands than driving clear across the Valley for somebody else's schedule.
Exactly. I was home in time to eat with your mom and look at Maya's science board on video.
I wrote down the gas estimate to Silver City. If we go, it works better after my Friday shift than trying to leave early.
Good. I will price tires before we promise anything.
Marlene sounded glad on the phone last week, but she said not to push the truck if it is acting up.
She has heard that engine complain enough times to know.
Mrs. Ito asked if you still have her hedge trimmer. She said no hurry, just wanted to know which porch it is on.
It is in our shed, second shelf. I will take it over after breakfast and send her a picture of where I left it.
Thank you. She also said their alley light is flickering again.
I will let Earl know too. He usually checks that side when he rolls his trash bin out.
Hall lady asked if you could add drywall anchors next time. Guess the faucet bit was a hit.
I can do anchors. I still have the demo board in the garage and a coffee can of bad examples.
You want me to print more handouts or just bring the donuts?
Handouts, please. Donuts if you want. I am keeping it simple: show them, answer questions, go home with my knee still speaking to me.
Too windy for a ride. I can drop that spare clamp by your place instead.
Good. I will be out front pulling goatheads and cutting back the prickly pear that is leaning into the walkway.
Leave room on that bench, old man. Last time I set a part down on a box of patio lights.
I cleared one corner yesterday. The other side still has Linda's fall decorations and the cooler.
Dad, can you hop on after dinner? Jake wants to ask you which wrench to use on that little bike brake.
Yes. Have him put the bike where there is light, not in the garage shadow.
Got it. He already lined up three wrong wrenches on purpose to test you.
That sounds like him. I will get my glasses so I can see what he is pointing at.
I am off at 3 if Dr. K keeps the last crown seat on time. We can leave from Vail right after.
No rush. Brian said he can bring Tyler and Mia earlier, so we will only be waiting on you, Noah, and Sophie.
Perfect. Please keep Sophie away from Brian's gauges this time. She still thinks they are toys.
I will put them on the high shelf before the crew gets here.
Mom said you disappeared after the insurance call. Everything okay?
I'm fine. I went out back and sanded those toy tool handles smooth. Sharpened the block plane too.
The boys would love one of those little sets, but please don't turn it into an order form.
They can have the finished one when you visit. If someone insists on paying for another later, that's their problem, not my calendar.
Did you make it to Dr. Patel this morning? I wrote down the questions you told me so you would not forget.
Yes. He said keep the small daily one the same and bring the home cuff numbers next visit.
Good. And what did he say about that spring shot they keep mentioning?
He said check the county page Monday and the pharmacist can match it to my record. I used the elevator there because the steps were making that right side complain.
Found that Chris LeDoux one where he jokes before the song. Sending it before I lose it again.
Got it. I will put it in my save pile with the rodeo stuff.
Better than watching trail dust blow across the porch today.
I may cast it after dinner if Linda is not using the TV.
Kids are asking if the little shelf can still get stain today. I told them no shortcuts.
They can wipe it down at 2:00 if the dust is gone. Make them show me the corners before the rag comes out.
Jace said you always check the back even though nobody sees it.
Especially the back. If your name is on it, do it square.
You need me to bring extra chairs tomorrow or is it the usual setup?
Usual. Linda and I have the small table set, then we will pull folding chairs when you all get here.
Got it. I found that old picture from '95 where you two are standing by the grill. Mom wants a copy?
Yes. She said it can go with the cards from that year in the hallway box.
I put the blue pack back in the freezer and the heating pad by your chair.
Thanks. I did the calf stretches before dinner and took two with the meatloaf.
Good. Tomorrow let's do the neighborhood blocks, not the wash path.
Agreed. I would rather go shorter than sit out all week.
Made coffee and looked at your photo. That ridge still turns pink just like when we were kids.
It was worth getting out before the streets got warm. Linda had me home in time to water the peppers.
Mama would laugh at you babying those plants.
She would also ask if the game starts at 1:10 or 6:40, so I checked.
If you two ever swing this way, White Sands is worth the extra morning. I can mail you my motel note.
Send it. Linda also has Monument Valley circled, but those are pencil marks for now.
Pencil is fine. Wait until the envelope has enough for rooms and gas.
That's the rule here. Map first, then cash, then keys.
I found the copied page from Aunt Ruth's Bible. It has McKee, Campbell, and Lancaster written in the margin.
That sounds like the page Erin wanted. I couldn't have named half of those without you.
I'll mail you a photo. Also, on the senior center signup, I put yours the way Mom always did on the first two check boxes.
Good. If it matches the old paperwork, that's fine by me.
I put the photo of Dad by the old truck where the cousins can see it. Linda should be able to find it.
I found it. That led me to a whole string of old steel-guitar clips from the fairgrounds days.
That sounds like you. Did you see the Silver City music night listed for next Friday?
Yes, it was right under the family pictures. I marked it in case we head that way later this month.
I found that old photo of Dad fixing the cracked handle on the post hole digger. Do you want it for your pages?
Yes, send it. I can use it near the part about keeping handles oiled and not tossing tools after one bad season.
Sent. I also remember Mom telling us not to pull up the little yellow flowers just because they looked dry.
That fits. I have a note saying some of the rough-looking plants are doing work you do not see.
That old Yamaha coughed twice then quit again. You still think float needle?
Could be. Drain the bowl into a clear cup first. If it is varnish, no sense ordering a coil.
I'll wait till you come by. Last time you saved me from buying half the machine.
Bring gloves and a tray for the screws. We will keep gas off the driveway and I will tell you before anything costs more than lunch money.
Trail by Bulldog looked dry and dusty today. You still thinking Monday?
Only if we roll early. I'm not sitting out there after it starts baking the seat.
Fair. Wear the ugly hat. Mine saved my neck last ride.
Hat, long shirt, and the boots that already have half that trail on them.
Weather app says 91 by 11 tomorrow. Still want Bulldog, or are we acting our age?
Bulldog if we unload at 6:20 and make it the short loop.
Fine by me. I will bring an extra jug. You bring that wide hat so Linda does not blame me.
Deal. If either of us starts fading at the wash, we turn around.
Dad, tire place quoted me $397 for the truck last month. If yours comes in close, don’t let them sell you extras.
I’ve got room for a number like that if it has to happen. I’d still rather catch it after I finish tonight’s receipts.
Fair. Your yellow pad still beat the shop guy’s computer last time.
Yellow pad plus the file on the laptop. One catches what the other misses.
We can make it by 4:30 if the kids finish their homework before we leave Tucson. Should I bring the salad or just dessert?
Dessert is easiest. Linda already started beans, and Brian said he is handling ice this time.
Good. If you and Mom still want those two seats at the community playhouse later this month, send me the date before I book our next visit.
Will do. She kept the flyer on the fridge so I don't forget.
Mom sent me the scan from the hallway wall. Was that you at 16 by the front step with Aunt Marlene sitting on the cooler?
Yes. That was the Apache Junction house. Dad must have come home straight from the bay because his shirt was still black at the cuffs.
Grandma is holding a stack of lunch trays in the next picture. I had not seen that one.
Marlene remembers where every picture was taken. I just remember the screen door sticking.
Are we still leaving by 9:35 for Mesa View? I put the checkbook and your worn brown book by the keys.
Yes. I marked that page Pastor Rob mentioned last time.
Good. Maybe after lunch we can drive Apache Trail a little and let your knee stretch before heading home.
That would be nice. The quiet out there sticks with me longer than the news does.
If you and Linda come up this way first, I still have that booklet from Fort Bayard. You liked the old photos last time.
Bring it out if we swing through Silver City. I am making a folder for the northern trip too.
The one with the trading post pages? I can copy the map notes before I forget.
Yes, please. Linda said she would rather have two good stops than six rushed ones.
Trailhead at 7 next Sunday? I will bring jerky. The guys may hang around after with their cooler and other nonsense.
Ride sounds good. I will bring coffee and waters. If the after part turns into that, I will head out.
Same old Keith. One sandwich, one cold bottle maybe, then home before the younger crowd gets weird.
That is enough for me. I want the truck straight and my head straight on the 60.
You firing up the smoker for the game or doing the sensible thing?
Sensible tonight. Chili pot, beans already soaked, and chicken from yesterday can go into tortillas.
Save me from myself. I saw brisket at the meat counter and kept walking.
I will do a small one when Brian comes over. The Bashas' 60+ tag knocked a few dollars off last time, so I watch for that.
Keith, I found that old folder from Mom's file cabinet. Do you still keep house papers in the blue binder?
Yes. Blue binder has the escrow notice, tax bill, insurance, and the March payment coupon.
Good. When you send the budget page, include Linda's office hours and whatever comes from the accounts on the 15th.
Got it. There are no county letters in that stack, just bank and tax stuff.
I put your sample ballot by the coffee maker. Erin's printed note is clipped to the article from Sunday.
Thanks. I crossed off the loudmouths on both sides. I want the ones who can keep taxes sane and still answer straight on force complaints.
That sounds like you. Read the note before you mark anything, please.
I will. Erin made a fair point about listening first, even when I don't agree with every sentence.
Old Garcia on 6th asked if you still come out for door frames. I said probably not but I'd check.
Tell him I can point him to Raul or look at photos, but I am not loading the truck for that anymore.
Copy. Raul still using your miter stand?
Yes. He can keep it until April. I only need the small stuff for the hall table.
Before we leave for groceries, can you put the Mesa copy in the glove box? I do not want it sliding around with the receipts.
Already in the folder. I added the old Apache Trail envelope too.
Good. And please take the water jug. The forecast says 86 by noon, and that parking lot has no shade.
Got it. Hat, jug, and the folder. Same routine as running errands with Dad, minus his busted pickup.
I am closing up the office. Please leave the porch light on and do not start the game yet.
Porch light is on. I saved your half of the salad and put one plate in the microwave.
Thank you. If we do even the short loop after I change shoes, I think we will both be out faster tonight. 🙂
I will wait. Shoes are by the back door and the TV can pause.
Made it home safe. I forgot to ask if you found the tan wrap you wanted before your ride.
Found it in the truck box. Mike and I are only doing the flatter side tomorrow.
Good. You can still have your desert morning without proving anything.
That's the plan. Half day, wrap on, home before the heat stacks up.
How did your clinic visit turn out? Linda said you were re-reading the March bills before you went.
I found Dad's old note card that said 'look twice before you plug it in.' Made me think of your garage table.
That line is going at the top of the sheet. The boys last week stopped rushing once they had to point to each step.
Same old list from Dr. Nguyen: pressure numbers, knee, sleep better. Nothing new got added.
Good. When you start circling those papers, step away before you bark at somebody.
He would have liked that. Are the community hall people still talking about pairing the older guys with students?
I did yesterday. Shut the folder, went to the garage, played the Marty Robbins record.
Yes, slowly. I told them we need small jobs first: lamp cord, bad switch, loose spade connector. Nothing that gets anyone in over their head.
Before I forget again, Mom's green bowl is still in the top cabinet here. You said Linda liked that one.
She does. If we get over there, we can wrap it in towels and bring it back.
No rush. We had a good long talk on the 6th, so I just wanted to send the reminder before it slipped away.
I put it on my list. You always remember where everything from that house ended up.
You still got that rivet gun? I can pick it up after the trail meeting.
Yes. I put my initials and the number from the plate in my notebook first, then it is yours.
Fair. Text me if you want me to look at that padlock while I am there.
Bring your small bit set. I already told Earl you may be in the driveway.
Need me for that Lowe's run or are you hiding in the garage again?
Give me half an hour. The cedar planter needed one more pass and the hatchet edge was ugly.
Customer pickup before lunch? Kidding.
One neighbor might take it. That's enough. I don't want Saturday turning into receipts and measurements.
That carb issue on the tiller still acting up?
A little. I watched two short ones where the guy cleans the jet with a bread tie wire. Going to try that before buying parts.
Send me a pic before you tear it apart.
Will do. Also saw Erin added the kids' robotics photos, so I may get pulled into a grandpa question first.
Dad, the paragraph you sent reads better when you start with the 2 bottles per person part, then the shade stops.
Good catch. I moved the loose-rock warning after that too, so it is not buried.
And maybe soften the line about newcomers. Say what to do instead of sounding mad.
Fair. I changed it to carry bags back, stay on the path, and leave the wash cleaner than you found it.
For tomorrow, I counted Tyler, Mia, Noah, and Sophie for dessert cups. Do we still have enough paper plates?
Yes. Brian texted that his first call is in east Mesa, so he may be late.
Erin said the office phones were already busy yesterday, but she still wants to drive up if they get out on time.
I will keep the food warm and leave the side gate open for whoever pulls in first.
I wiped the front camera on your tablet. It was all fingerprints again.
Thank you. Nate said I looked foggy last Saturday.
I also moved the lamp so they can see your face instead of the ceiling fan.
Good. I need both hands free if Lily asks about the birdhouse hinges.
For Sunday, should I set out the blue platter or just the plain plates?
Plain plates. I am slicing the brisket thin and putting more beans and salad on the table.
Good. I also found the receipt from the last Fry's trip. The 55+ line came off after the coupons.
Nice. Monday can be eggs and toast, then the leftover meat goes into tacos Tuesday.
I left the TV remote by your chair. The red app is still open from your porch songs.
Thanks. It started suggesting more with Denver and the fellows in pearl snaps.
Just keep it low if you are going to play another one. I am reading in bed.
Will do. I only wanted to finish the one from the late show set.
The back step at church feels loose again. I remembered how you used to tap around before deciding what board was bad.
Have them rope it off until someone checks the stringer. A loose tread can fool you if the nail heads look fine.
I'll tell Pastor Jim. He asked if you would guess a price from a picture.
Picture first, price after I see what is under it. No guessing somebody into a bill.
Want me to bring the kids by after I finish that thermostat call?
Come around 5. I already rubbed the chicken and there are beans left from last night.
Nice. I will bring tortillas. You using the old grill or did it finally retire?
Old grill still has one more round in it. I am doing onions and cactus strips too, so do not let them fill up on fries.
Dad, if you're taking the truck past Kayenta, check the spare before you go. That stretch eats bad tires.
Already on my list. I am not dragging your mom down every goat path, just the paved side roads that make sense.
Good. Mom will tolerate your sign-reading stops better if the AC works and the road is not washboard.
Fair trade. I will do belts and hoses this week, then she can pick which old stop gets the longer break.
For Easter dinner, should I bring a mixed pack or just tea and sparkling water for your cooler?
Tea and sparkling water are plenty. I still have one brown bottle left from Brian's cookout.
Got it. Also Mom asked me to keep the neighbor's homemade candy away from the kids' table until she checks what is in it.
Good idea. I will keep my plate simple and stay on dishwasher duty.
I finished the theater volunteer form. I used your usual answers on the background section and skipped the family-origin question since it was optional.
Thanks. If they need more, they can ask, but I don't have much beyond what Marlene keeps in that envelope.
I wrote down Moore, McKee, and Lancaster on a sticky for Erin, not on the form.
That's plenty. I never did chase those lines very far.
After supper, could you look at the grill starter? The chicken is already marinating.
I will. I need to put the mower battery on the charger first and then we can do the receipts.
Thank you. Please do not stack the grocery tubs in front of your pegboard again. I nearly tripped.
Fair. I will shift them after I coil the hose by the sage.
I found Mom's AJ High yearbook and Dad's folded program from the same gym. Do you want copies?
Yes, please. Linda is making a folder for the kids with the carport pictures and those papers.
I will mark the one where my little room had the pink curtains. You can see your toolbox shelf in the hallway.
Funny how that small hallway held half our stuff.
Clouds look decent. Bulldog Canyon or just the easy run by the fence line?
Fence line. One loop, coffee after. I am not doing the rocky climb today.
Copy that. I strapped my brace on too, so no hero riding from either of us.
Works for me. I want to be able to stand at the bench this afternoon.
Did you ever decide on the school crossing item? I know we see that one differently sometimes.
I read the whole booklet section. I can back safer corners, but I want the tax part written clean and not buried.
Fair. Just don't skip the judge bios again because they are boring.
Already done. Linda watched me put the last page in the sleeve after dinner.
Dad, before you answer the pharmacy text, can you look at the county page I sent? It has the March update in plain English.
The kids asked if you still help people fix phone contacts on Tuesdays. They remember that room from when we stopped by.
I read it after supper. I will ask the pharmacist when I pick up Linda's toothpaste and my refill Friday.
Still Tuesdays, and sometimes Thursdays if Marta gets a bigger sign-up list.
That explains why Mom said you were cutting cardstock after dinner again.
Good. Also Brian said you were limping after moving those pavers. Please let him grab the rest.
Only 20 sheets. I am better at trimming those than explaining cloud backups.
I will. Brace is by the back door, and I am doing the easy stretch Dr. Patel showed me.
You taking that Gilbert bathroom tear-out? Heard it's good money but starts at 6 every day.
Nope. Too much freeway and I'd miss the Thursday table. I told Joe I can do small repairs this side of Power Rd.
Bring the stripped valve demo today. Those guys loved watching you fight that thing last time.
Already in the truck. Funny how having a place to be by ten makes the morning go smoother.
I may swing by the senior center first, then head over. Save me a chair if Ray's crew fills up.
I'll get there before six-thirty. Same corner if nobody beats us to it.
Also don't answer Carl's post. He tagged half the county and wants somebody to bite.
Saw it. I'm leaving it alone and bringing the good pencils instead.
Chief's follow-up was better than I expected. Still a lot of folks yelling from the back row.
Yeah. I liked the part about publishing the camera audit numbers. Didn't like the guy saying scrap the whole department and start over.
You're picking the boring lane again: fix the gear, train people, fire the bad ones.
Boring usually works. Erin will still tell me I missed something, so I'll call her after dinner.
We are stopping in Casa Grande for gas. Do you need us to bring anything for tomorrow?
No, I have chicken marinating and a bowl of salsa made. Linda found good squash and peppers.
Perfect. The kids asked if you are making those cactus pieces again.
I trimmed them already. We will keep it simple on the patio, beans on the side, and no drive-thru bags.
I posted the band concert pictures. Mom said you were looking for the one where Leo has the trumpet up too high.
Found it. While I was there I saw the library swap meet notice and the Lost Dutchman trail update.
Good, just don't click every suggested old concert clip or dinner will be cold.
Too late, one from 1976 was already playing while I looked up how to square that little shelf.
Mom said you were out before the school buses again. Did you actually take water this time?
Two bottles, and I wore the big hat you all make fun of.
Good. I am not teasing if it works. Did you do the whole ridge?
No, just to the first marker and back. Enough for one morning.
I finished the March bills. Nothing came in from the old yellow pad again, so I moved that folder to the back of the drawer.
Good place for it. I only used the pad once this month to write screw sizes for the hall group.
That makes the checking account easier to read. Please save the receipts for the hinges and outlet covers, just so we know what came out of groceries.
I put your washed shirt on the chair, the loose white one. Please take the cap when you go by Ace.
Thanks. I'll wear that and the boots from the garage since I'm loading bags of soil.
They are clipped by the coffee maker. I will keep next Saturday's list shorter.
Those boots still have red dust on them from Mike's ride.
Then they're already broken in for today's mess.
I put the two finished shelves by the back door. The birdhouse with the green roof is still drying on newspaper.
Thanks. Leave the names penciled underneath. They did the work, so they should see it there.
Maya asked if you will come to her school thing Tuesday. I told her we would check the calendar.
Put it down for me. Boards can wait. I don't want her looking around and thinking I forgot.
The Oak Creek room emailed one more discount. Do you want me to hold it?
Let it pass. Tires and the prescription run used more than I figured this week.
Then we will keep the blue envelope going and look at Monument Valley after dinner.
Good. I'll print the gas-stop sheet instead of opening airline prices.
Mrs. Haney left a thank-you note on the porch. She said the hallway light finally stays on.
Good. It was the loose neutral in the box, not the fixture. I wrote what I found on her receipt.
I put the April budget printout in the drawer so we can do it after our walk, not before dinner.
She also said you swept the entry. That made her smile.
Fair. I already looked at the calendar twice and got snippy about the electric estimate.
Drywall dust travels. I shut the breaker, checked it twice, and charged her only for the hour.
Then garage first, walk second. The clinic papers only asked you to keep routines steady, and that one works.
Putting the Eagles on now. I'll meet you by the front door at 7:10.
The kids saw your picture from this morning and asked why the hills looked orange.
Tell them it only lasts a few minutes if you get out early enough.
They also want to know if Grandpa is still coming over after the D-backs game tomorrow.
Yes. I will bring the little shovel too, if they still want to start that planter box.
I put the two diploma sleeves beside the photo of your dad's name patch. The plastic is brittle, so please leave them flat.
Will do. I also found Mom's old cafeteria badge in the same shoebox.
That shoebox has Marlene's school picture tucked behind your 16th birthday photo too.
Keep it all together. That box pretty much tells the old AJ story.
Dinner can wait a little. I heard the sander and guessed you needed a few quiet minutes.
Just finishing the walnut board and putting an edge back on the small knife. Music is helping.
Mrs. Hanley left an envelope for the last board. I put it by the coffee tin.
Thanks. Tell her no more until I have extra scraps and feel like making another.
Did you ever find the Back Home Again clip you were hunting for?
Yes, from a TV broadcast with the camera pulled way back. Took some scrolling.
Send it when you get a minute. I want to show it to Ray after lunch.
I sent the link. There is another one beside it with LeDoux doing This Cowboy's Hat.
Did you and Linda make it to that Mesa View place this month? I found Mama's old note card with the verse she liked.
We made it a couple Sundays. Rob's message was plainspoken, which I like.
That sounds like you. Do you still go sit by the Superstitions when the sun first comes up?
When the knee allows it. That morning hush does me good.
Made it back to Silver City safe. I left the photo copies on your kitchen table under the salt shaker.
Thanks. The one by the wash brought back more than I expected.
I remember Mom saying everything important started with a drive west from Mesa, then it was mostly dirt, chores, and looking at the Superstitions every morning.
That tracks. You learned early to keep a spare belt, extra water, and a shovel where you could reach them.
Mom said you two were doing the kitchen table stack tonight. I can send the dental receipt photo before you start if that helps.
Send it over. I’ll put it with gas, groceries, and Linda’s refill slip before I open the bank page.
Sent. And please don’t dip into that $400 unless the tire really fails.
Got it. I’ll put the photo in the laptop file and note the same amount in the little book.
I moved the roast to the lower shelf so the kids can reach the juice boxes. Brian said he may be ten minutes late.
I'll set out the extra plates after I sweep the patio. Tell Erin the little ones can use the card table.
Thank you. Also, the Chase Field broadcast starts at 6:10, and the playhouse mailed next month's flyer today. We can look after everyone leaves. :)
Sounds right. One thing at a time: plates first, then the game, then the flyer.

Glad you made it. Those will get used. The little cooler still has two bottles from the whole month.
That sounds like you. Uncle Dale kept offering his tins after dinner and you kept walking out to check the porch light.
Porch light needed checking more than I needed any of that.
Made it home safe. That photo Linda sent of you by the trail sign was a nice one.
We only did the first overlook. I stopped while it was still a good idea.

Yes, and the cold pack. I still got an hour at the bench before supper.
